metadata.title: Universal Two-Parent Heritage Compatibility Registry
metadata.closure_rule: Compatibility is repeatedly propagated through the race graph until stable. If A is compatible with B and B is compatible with C, A and C are compatible unless a body-plan or explicit pair exclusion overrides the path.

rule_precedence: Body-plan and explicit pair exclusions override all other rules.
Two direct biological races in the same creator category are compatible.
All direct biological humanoid-compatible peoples are compatible.
The listed creator-family bridges directly connect every qualifying creation in both families.
The listed subtype/race seed bridges add their exact genetic links.
Transitive closure repeats all valid links until no additional pairings are added.
A same-category pairing involving a non-biological body plan is assisted, not ordinary biological progeny.
user_logic_restatement: Only two direct parents are modeled.
Different races in one creator category can have progeny when both are direct biological parents.
Two different bloodlines, lineages, or ancestries of the same parent race can have progeny.
All direct biological humanoids can mix.
Nebyrr's creations directly mix with the direct biological creations of Sigrananna, Marduthor, Ishtanora, Enkirael, Anubaldir, and Thalunesh.
Sea Elf compatibility seeds links to Merfolk and Tamhiogal.
Lizardfolk compatibility seeds links to Grung and every Dril'thar bloodline; same-category and transitive rules carry that connection through Bastveig's biological family.
Anything admitted into a compatible genetic family can mix with the other members of that family unless an explicit exclusion overrides it.

subtype_and_race_seed_bridges.details: Sea Elves and Merfolk can have biological progeny.
Sea Elves and Tamhiogals can have biological progeny.
Lizardfolk and Dril'thars are explicitly compatible; every Dril'thar bloodline participates.
Lizardfolk and Grung are explicitly compatible.

subtype_rules.same_parent_race: A same-parent mixed heritage requires two different subtypes whose subtype_type is bloodline, lineage, or ancestry.
subtype_rules.forms: Forms and castes can be recorded as phenotype expressions but do not count as genetic bloodlines. Jaspey forms therefore cannot produce a Jaspey × Jaspey bloodline heritage.
subtype_rules.different_parent_races: Selected subtypes remain the two direct parents’ ancestry expressions. Parent-race compatibility controls whether the pairing is biological, assisted, or incompatible.
subtype_rules.transitive_subtype_bridge: A subtype bridge can connect its parent race to another race because all bloodlines/lineages/ancestries of the same parent race can mix; closure then repeats outward.

inheritance_reference.title: Parent-to-Child Genetics: Direct Inheritance Without Grandparents
inheritance_reference.rule: Only the two direct genetic parents are modeled. Grandparents, earlier ancestors, pedigrees, ancestry percentages, and grandparent phenotypes are ignored.
inheritance_reference.fifty_fifty_rule: A child receives one haploid nuclear chromosome set from each parent, commonly summarized as roughly 50 percent of nuclear DNA from each. This does not mean that every visible trait is an exact 50/50 blend.
inheritance_reference.phenotype_rule: A phenotype is produced by genotype plus gene regulation, interactions among genes, development, environment, age, chance, penetrance, and expressivity.
inheritance_reference.variation_rule: Independent assortment, crossing over, random fertilization, gene interactions, and new variants make each conception genetically distinct.
inheritance_reference.mixed_heritage_rule: Do not treat a mixed-heritage child as a visual 50/50 morph. Define loci, developmental interactions, and expression rules. Some traits may be inherited discretely, some codominantly, some polygenically, some not at all, and some may be incompatible or species-specific.
